# `silk/xml/document`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

Parse an XML 1.0 document into an owned, namespace-aware tree of elements, text, comments, and
processing instructions.

## When to use
Use [`XmlDocument.parse`](#XmlDocument.impl.parse) to read a complete XML document, such as an SVG image, a feed, or a
configuration file, from bytes. Use [`XmlDocument.parseWithLimits`](#XmlDocument.impl.parseWithLimits) to lower the resource limits
for input that you do not trust. Walk the tree from [`XmlDocument.root`](#XmlDocument.impl.root) with
[`XmlDocument.firstChild`](#XmlDocument.impl.firstChild) and [`XmlDocument.nextSibling`](#XmlDocument.impl.nextSibling), read names with
[`XmlDocument.localName`](#XmlDocument.impl.localName) and [`XmlDocument.namespaceUri`](#XmlDocument.impl.namespaceUri), and read attributes with
[`XmlDocument.attribute`](#XmlDocument.impl.attribute). Use [`XmlPseudoAttributes.parse`](#XmlPseudoAttributes.impl.parse) to read the pseudo-attributes of an
`xml-stylesheet` processing instruction.

## Details
The parser follows XML 1.0 (Fifth Edition) and Namespaces in XML 1.0, and does not validate.
It accepts UTF-8 and UTF-16 input, with or without a byte order mark, and checks the encoding
declaration. It reads the internal DTD subset: general and parameter entities, attribute
defaults, and ID attributes. It never fetches an external subset or an external entity. It skips
their content, and [`XmlDocument.skippedExternalContent`](#XmlDocument.impl.skippedExternalContent) reports that it did.
[`XmlDocument.skippedEntities`](#XmlDocument.impl.skippedEntities) identifies unread references. [`XmlDocument.notations`](#XmlDocument.impl.notations) and
[`XmlDocument.unparsedEntities`](#XmlDocument.impl.unparsedEntities) expose DTD metadata without fetching external resources.

All nodes live in one arena in the document and are addressed by [`XmlNodeId`](#XmlNodeId). The document
stores names, namespace URIs, text, and attribute values as normalized UTF-8, and the accessors
return `string` views that borrow the document. Line ends are normalized to `\n`, character and
entity references are replaced, and attribute values are normalized as XML requires. CDATA
sections become text nodes. Comments, processing instructions, namespace declarations, and
attributes in foreign namespaces are kept.

## Errors
- `XmlError` if the input is not well-formed, breaks a namespace rule, or exceeds an
  [`XmlLimits`](#XmlLimits) bound. `reason` names the problem and `offset` gives its position. No partial
  document is returned.
- `OutOfMemoryError` if the `Allocator` cannot supply the document.

## Gotchas
An `XmlError` offset counts bytes of the decoded UTF-8 text with normalized line ends, not bytes
of the input, except for an encoding error, whose offset counts input bytes. For UTF-16 input or
input with `\r\n` line ends, the two differ.

## Examples
### Count the children of the root that have an `id` attribute
```silk
import silk.core.effect { Effect }
import silk.core.option { Option }
import silk.mem.allocator { Allocator, OutOfMemoryError }
import silk.xml.document { XmlDocument, XmlError, XmlNodeId, XmlNodeKind }

pub effect fn main() -> i32
  ! XmlError | OutOfMemoryError {
  let mut allocator = Allocator.systemAllocatorProvider()
  let source = b"<list><item id='a'/><item/><item id='c'>text</item></list>"
  let document = run XmlDocument.parse(source) |> Effect.provideMut<Allocator>(&mut allocator)
  let mut count = 0
  let mut child = document.firstChild(document.root())
  while let Option<XmlNodeId>.Some { value } = child {
    if document.kind(value) == XmlNodeKind.Element && document.attribute(value, "", "id").isSome() {
      count = count + 1
    }
    child = document.nextSibling(value)
  }
  if count != 2 || document.localName(document.root()) != "list" {
    return 1
  }
  return 0
}
```

### Read a namespaced attribute
```silk
import silk.core.effect { Effect }
import silk.core.option { Option }
import silk.mem.allocator { Allocator, OutOfMemoryError }
import silk.xml.document { XmlDocument, XmlError }

pub effect fn main() -> i32
  ! XmlError | OutOfMemoryError {
  let mut allocator = Allocator.systemAllocatorProvider()
  let source = b"<svg xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' xmlns:x='http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink' x:href='#a'/>"
  let document = run XmlDocument.parse(source) |> Effect.provideMut<Allocator>(&mut allocator)
  let root = document.root()
  let href = document.attribute(root, "http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink", "href")
    |> Option<string>.unwrapOr("")
  if href != "#a" || document.namespaceUri(root) != "http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" {
    return 1
  }
  return 0
}
```

<a id="XmlLimits"></a>

## `XmlLimits`

```silk
pub struct XmlLimits
```

The resource bounds of one XML parse.

### When to use

Use [`XmlLimits.make`](#XmlLimits.impl.make) for the defaults, which suit untrusted input, and lower a field before
you pass the limits to [`XmlDocument.parseWithLimits`](#XmlDocument.impl.parseWithLimits) or [`XmlPseudoAttributes.parse`](#XmlPseudoAttributes.impl.parse).

### Details

When the input exceeds a bound, the parse fails with [`XmlReason.Limit`](#XmlReason.Limit) and returns no
document.

### Gotchas

`maxDepth` and `maxEntityDepth` can only lower the hard ceilings of 256 and 32. A larger value
has no effect.

<a id="XmlDocument"></a>

## `XmlDocument`

```silk
pub struct XmlDocument
```

A parsed XML document: an arena of nodes and the UTF-8 text of their names and values.

### When to use

Use [`XmlDocument.parse`](#XmlDocument.impl.parse) or [`XmlDocument.parseWithLimits`](#XmlDocument.impl.parseWithLimits) to make one. Walk it from
[`XmlDocument.root`](#XmlDocument.impl.root) with [`XmlDocument.firstChild`](#XmlDocument.impl.firstChild) and [`XmlDocument.nextSibling`](#XmlDocument.impl.nextSibling), or visit
every node in document order with [`XmlDocument.nodes`](#XmlDocument.impl.nodes).

### Details

Every name, namespace URI, text, and attribute value is a `string` view that borrows the
document, so none of them can outlive it. Namespace prefixes are resolved: every element and
attribute has a local name and a namespace URI, which is empty for no namespace. Nodes are
stored in document order.

<a id="XmlDocument.impl.skippedEntities"></a>

### Method `skippedEntities`

```silk
pub fn skippedEntities(self: &XmlDocument) -> &[XmlSkippedEntity]
```

Borrows notifications for unread entity references in declarations, attributes, and content.
Each entry gives the entity name and the normalized byte offset. A skipped reference supplies
no replacement text. External subset declarations are reported by `skippedExternalContent`.

<a id="XmlDocument.impl.notations"></a>

### Method `notations`

```silk
pub fn notations(self: &XmlDocument) -> &[XmlNotation]
```

Borrows notation declarations read from the internal DTD, in declaration order.
Public identifiers have collapsed whitespace. System identifiers retain their spelling.
Declarations in unread external content are absent.

<a id="XmlDocument.impl.unparsedEntities"></a>

### Method `unparsedEntities`

```silk
pub fn unparsedEntities(self: &XmlDocument) -> &[XmlUnparsedEntity]
```

Borrows unparsed entity declarations read from the internal DTD, in declaration order.
The first declaration of each entity binds. No external content is fetched.

<a id="XmlDocument.impl.parse"></a>

### Associated function `parse`

```silk
pub effect fn parse(data: &[u8]) -> XmlDocument
    ! XmlError | OutOfMemoryError
    ? &mut Allocator
```

Parses `data` as a complete XML document with the default [`XmlLimits`](#XmlLimits).

#### When to use

Use this function for input of ordinary size. Use [`XmlDocument.parseWithLimits`](#XmlDocument.impl.parseWithLimits) to set
tighter bounds.

#### Details

`data` is UTF-8 or UTF-16. A byte order mark, or the first character `<`, selects the
encoding. The parse reads the internal DTD subset and never fetches external content. The
defaults allow 16 MiB of input, 64 MiB of retained text, 8 MiB of entity expansion, one
million nodes, attributes, and declarations, element depth 256, and entity depth 32.

#### Errors

- `XmlError` if `data` is not a well-formed, namespace-well-formed XML 1.0 document or
  exceeds a default limit. `reason` gives the cause and `offset` the position. No document is
  returned.
- `OutOfMemoryError` if the `Allocator` cannot supply the document.

<a id="XmlDocument.impl.parseWithLimits"></a>

### Associated function `parseWithLimits`

```silk
pub effect fn parseWithLimits(data: &[u8], limits: &XmlLimits) -> XmlDocument
    ! XmlError | OutOfMemoryError
    ? &mut Allocator
```

Parses `data` as a complete XML document, within the bounds of `limits`.

#### When to use

Use this function for untrusted input where the default bounds of [`XmlDocument.parse`](#XmlDocument.impl.parse) are
too large, such as an upload size limit.

#### Details

`data` is UTF-8 or UTF-16. A byte order mark, or the first character `<`, selects the
encoding. The parse reads the internal DTD subset and never fetches external content.

#### Errors

- `XmlError` with [`XmlReason.Limit`](#XmlReason.Limit) if the input exceeds a bound of `limits`.
- `XmlError` with another kind if `data` is not a well-formed, namespace-well-formed XML 1.0
  document. `offset` gives the position. No document is returned.
- `OutOfMemoryError` if the `Allocator` cannot supply the document.

#### Gotchas

`maxDepth` and `maxEntityDepth` can only lower the hard ceilings of 256 and 32.

<a id="XmlDocument.impl.nodes"></a>

### Method `nodes`

```silk
pub fn nodes(self: &XmlDocument) -> &[XmlNode]
```

Returns every node of the document in document order, indexed by [`XmlNodeId`](#XmlNodeId).

#### When to use

Use this function to visit every node without walking the tree, or to read the
[`XmlNodeKind`](#XmlNodeKind) and parent of a node.

#### Details

The node at index `id.index` is the node with that id. A node comes after its parent and
before its next sibling. The slice includes comments and processing instructions outside the
root element.

<a id="XmlDocument.impl.skippedExternalContent"></a>

### Method `skippedExternalContent`

```silk
pub fn skippedExternalContent(self: &XmlDocument) -> bool
```

Returns `true` if the document declares an external DTD subset or an external entity whose
content the parse skipped.

#### When to use

Use this function to tell if the document can depend on declarations that the parse did not
read, such as an entity or an attribute default in an external subset.

#### Details

The parser never fetches external content. A skipped entity reference produces no replacement
text or node. `skippedEntities` identifies unread references, including references in attributes.
Attribute values can therefore be incomplete when this function returns `true`.

<a id="XmlDocument.impl.firstChild"></a>

### Method `firstChild`

```silk
pub fn firstChild(self: &XmlDocument, id: XmlNodeId) -> Option<XmlNodeId>
```

Returns the first child of node `id`, or `None` if it has no children or `id` is out of
range.

#### Details

Only elements have children. The children are elements, text, comments, and processing
instructions, in document order.

<a id="XmlDocument.impl.nextSibling"></a>

### Method `nextSibling`

```silk
pub fn nextSibling(self: &XmlDocument, id: XmlNodeId) -> Option<XmlNodeId>
```

Returns the node after `id` that has the same parent, or `None` if `id` is the last child or
out of range.

#### Gotchas

The root element and the comments and processing instructions outside it have no parent and
are not linked as siblings. Read them with [`XmlDocument.nodes`](#XmlDocument.impl.nodes).

#### When to use

Use this function to report a name to a person. Compare names with
[`XmlDocument.localName`](#XmlDocument.impl.localName) and [`XmlDocument.namespaceUri`](#XmlDocument.impl.namespaceUri), because the prefix of a namespace
can change between documents.

#### Details

The result is empty for text, for comments, and for an id that is out of range. It borrows
the document.

<a id="XmlDocument.impl.namespaceUri"></a>

### Method `namespaceUri`

```silk
pub fn namespaceUri<'a>(self: &'a XmlDocument, id: XmlNodeId) -> string<'a>
```

Returns the namespace URI of element `id`, or an empty string if the element is in no
namespace.

#### Details

The URI comes from the prefix of the element, or from the default namespace in scope for an
unprefixed element. The result is empty for other node kinds and for an id that is out of
range. It borrows the document.

<a id="XmlDocument.impl.text"></a>

### Method `text`

```silk
pub fn text<'a>(self: &'a XmlDocument, id: XmlNodeId) -> string<'a>
```

Returns the text of a text, comment, or processing instruction node.

#### Details

For a text node, the result has references replaced and line ends normalized to `\n`. For a
processing instruction, it is the content after the target and its white space. The result is
empty for an element and for an id that is out of range. It borrows the document.

#### Gotchas

The text of an element is in its child text nodes. Adjacent text, CDATA sections, and
references can form more than one text node.

<a id="XmlDocument.impl.byteLength"></a>

### Method `byteLength`

```silk
pub fn byteLength(self: &XmlDocument) -> usize
```

Returns the number of bytes of UTF-8 that the document holds for names, namespace URIs,
text, and attribute values.

#### Details

The count includes values that [`XmlDocument.setAttribute`](#XmlDocument.impl.setAttribute) replaced, until
[`XmlDocument.restore`](#XmlDocument.impl.restore) drops them.

<a id="XmlDocument.impl.attributeCount"></a>

### Method `attributeCount`

```silk
pub fn attributeCount(self: &XmlDocument) -> usize
```

Returns the number of attributes on all elements of the document, including attributes that
come from DTD defaults.

<a id="XmlDocument.impl.attributes"></a>

### Method `attributes`

```silk
pub fn attributes(self: &XmlDocument, id: XmlNodeId) -> &[XmlAttribute]
```

Returns the attributes of element `id` in source order, followed by the attributes that come
from DTD defaults.

#### Details

The result includes namespace declarations, such as `xmlns` and `xmlns:x`, whose namespace
URI is `http://www.w3.org/2000/xmlns/`. It is empty for other node kinds and for an id that is
out of range.

<a id="XmlDocument.impl.attributeLocalName"></a>

### Method `attributeLocalName`

```silk
pub fn attributeLocalName<'a>(self: &'a XmlDocument, attr: XmlAttribute) -> string<'a>
```

Returns the local name of `attr`, without its prefix.

#### Details

`attr` must come from [`XmlDocument.attributes`](#XmlDocument.impl.attributes) of this document. The result is empty for an
attribute of another document that is out of range. It borrows the document.

<a id="XmlDocument.impl.attributeNamespaceUri"></a>

### Method `attributeNamespaceUri`

```silk
pub fn attributeNamespaceUri<'a>(self: &'a XmlDocument, attr: XmlAttribute) -> string<'a>
```

Returns the namespace URI of `attr`, or an empty string if it has no prefix.

#### Details

An unprefixed attribute is in no namespace, even when a default namespace is in scope.
`attr` must come from [`XmlDocument.attributes`](#XmlDocument.impl.attributes) of this document. The result borrows the
document.

<a id="XmlDocument.impl.attributeQualifiedName"></a>

### Method `attributeQualifiedName`

```silk
pub fn attributeQualifiedName<'a>(self: &'a XmlDocument, attr: XmlAttribute) -> string<'a>
```

Returns the name of `attr` as it is written in the source, with its prefix.

#### Details

`attr` must come from [`XmlDocument.attributes`](#XmlDocument.impl.attributes) of this document. The result borrows the
document.

<a id="XmlDocument.impl.attributeValue"></a>

### Method `attributeValue`

```silk
pub fn attributeValue<'a>(self: &'a XmlDocument, attr: XmlAttribute) -> string<'a>
```

Returns the normalized value of `attr`.

#### Details

References are replaced and white space is normalized as XML requires, including the extra
collapsing for attributes that the DTD declares with a type other than `CDATA`. `attr` must
come from [`XmlDocument.attributes`](#XmlDocument.impl.attributes) of this document. The result borrows the document.
An unread entity contributes no replacement text; `skippedEntities` reports the omitted reference.

<a id="XmlDocument.impl.attributeIsId"></a>

### Method `attributeIsId`

```silk
pub fn attributeIsId(self: &XmlDocument, attr: XmlAttribute) -> bool
```

Returns `true` if the DTD declares `attr` with type `ID`.

#### Details

The `xml:id` attribute is an ID only when the DTD declares it. `attr` must come from
[`XmlDocument.attributes`](#XmlDocument.impl.attributes) of this document.

<a id="XmlDocument.impl.attribute"></a>

### Method `attribute`

```silk
pub fn attribute<'a>(
    self: &'a XmlDocument,
    id: XmlNodeId,
    namespaceUri: string,
    localName: string,
  ) -> Option<string<'a>>
```

Returns the value of the attribute of element `id` with local name `localName` in namespace
`namespaceUri`, or `None` if the element does not have it.

#### Details

Pass an empty `namespaceUri` for an unprefixed attribute. The match uses the resolved
namespace URI, not the prefix in the source. The result borrows the document.

<a id="XmlDocument.impl-2"></a>

## Implementation `XmlDocument`

```silk
impl XmlDocument
```

<a id="XmlDocument.impl.setAttribute"></a>

### Method `setAttribute`

```silk
pub effect fn setAttribute(
    self: &mut XmlDocument,
    id: XmlNodeId,
    namespaceUri: string,
    localName: string,
    value: string,
  ) -> ()
    ! OutOfMemoryError
    ? &mut Allocator
```

Sets the attribute of element `id` with local name `localName` in namespace `namespaceUri`
to `value`, and adds the attribute if the element does not have it.

#### When to use

Use this function to apply computed values, such as animated attributes, to a parsed
document. Take an [`XmlSnapshot`](#XmlSnapshot) with [`XmlDocument.snapshot`](#XmlDocument.impl.snapshot) first and put it back with
[`XmlDocument.restore`](#XmlDocument.impl.restore) to undo the changes.

#### Details

A new attribute has no prefix, so its qualified name is `localName`, and it is not an ID.
Changing an attribute does not change which attributes are IDs. Nothing happens if `id` is
not an element.

#### Errors

- `OutOfMemoryError` if the `Allocator` cannot store the value. The attributes of the
  element can be unchanged or already changed.

#### Gotchas

The replaced value stays in the storage of the document, so repeated calls make the
document grow. [`XmlDocument.restore`](#XmlDocument.impl.restore) drops the replaced values.

<a id="XmlSnapshot"></a>

## `XmlSnapshot`

```silk
pub struct XmlSnapshot
```

The attribute state of an [`XmlDocument`](#XmlDocument) at one moment, taken with [`XmlDocument.snapshot`](#XmlDocument.impl.snapshot)
and put back with [`XmlDocument.restore`](#XmlDocument.impl.restore).

### When to use

Use a snapshot when you apply values with [`XmlDocument.setAttribute`](#XmlDocument.impl.setAttribute) many times, such as once
for each frame of an animation. Restore the snapshot before each round, so that rounds do not
see each other's values and the document does not grow with the number of rounds.

### Details

A snapshot owns a copy of the attribute list of the document. It does not borrow the document.

<a id="XmlDocument.impl-3"></a>

## Implementation `XmlDocument`

```silk
impl XmlDocument
```

<a id="XmlDocument.impl.snapshot"></a>

### Method `snapshot`

```silk
pub effect fn snapshot(self: &XmlDocument) -> XmlSnapshot
    ! OutOfMemoryError
    ? &mut Allocator
```

Returns an [`XmlSnapshot`](#XmlSnapshot) of the current attributes of every element.

#### Details

The snapshot copies the attribute list, so it costs memory proportional to the number of
attributes and nodes. Pass it to [`XmlDocument.restore`](#XmlDocument.impl.restore) to undo later calls to
[`XmlDocument.setAttribute`](#XmlDocument.impl.setAttribute).

#### Errors

- `OutOfMemoryError` if the `Allocator` cannot supply the copy. The document does not
  change.

<a id="XmlDocument.impl.restore"></a>

### Method `restore`

```silk
pub effect fn restore(self: &mut XmlDocument, snapshot: &XmlSnapshot) -> bool
    ! OutOfMemoryError
    ? &mut Allocator
```

Puts back the attributes recorded in `snapshot`, and drops every attribute value and name
that [`XmlDocument.setAttribute`](#XmlDocument.impl.setAttribute) stored since. Returns `false`, with no change, if
`snapshot` cannot come from this document.

#### Details

The storage of the document shrinks back to its size when the snapshot was taken. A snapshot
can be restored any number of times.

#### Errors

- `OutOfMemoryError` if the `Allocator` cannot supply the restored lists. The document can
  be partly restored. Restore the snapshot again to finish.

#### Gotchas

The check compares sizes only. A snapshot of another document with the same number of nodes
and no more storage passes the check and gives that document's attributes to this one.

<a id="XmlPseudoAttributes"></a>

## `XmlPseudoAttributes`

```silk
pub struct XmlPseudoAttributes
```

The pseudo-attributes of an `xml-stylesheet` processing instruction, such as `href` and
`type`, read with [`XmlPseudoAttributes.parse`](#XmlPseudoAttributes.impl.parse).

### Details

The set owns the decoded names and values. Look one up with [`XmlPseudoAttributes.get`](#XmlPseudoAttributes.impl.get).

<a id="XmlPseudoAttributes.impl"></a>

## Implementation `XmlPseudoAttributes`

```silk
impl XmlPseudoAttributes
```

<a id="XmlPseudoAttributes.impl.get"></a>

### Method `get`

```silk
pub fn get<'a>(self: &'a XmlPseudoAttributes, name: string) -> Option<string<'a>>
```

Returns the decoded value of pseudo-attribute `name`, or `None` if the set does not have it.

#### Details

Names are compared exactly, with case. The result borrows the set.

<a id="XmlPseudoAttributes.impl.parse"></a>

### Associated function `parse`

```silk
pub effect fn parse(data: string, limits: &XmlLimits) -> XmlPseudoAttributes
    ! XmlError | OutOfMemoryError
    ? &mut Allocator
```

Parses `data`, the text of an `xml-stylesheet` processing instruction, as pseudo-attributes.

#### When to use

Use this function on the result of [`XmlDocument.text`](#XmlDocument.impl.text) for a processing instruction whose
target is `xml-stylesheet`, to read the `href`, `type`, `media`, and other values that link
a style sheet to the document.

#### Details

The grammar is that of
[Associating Style Sheets with XML documents, Second Edition](https://www.w3.org/TR/xml-stylesheet/).
Each pseudo-attribute is an XML name, `=`, and a quoted value. Only character references and
the five predefined entity references are replaced, and white space in values is not
normalized. `limits` bounds the length of `data` (`maxInputBytes`), the stored names and
values (`maxStorageBytes`), the number of pseudo-attributes (`maxAttributes`), and the bytes
that references add (`maxExpandedBytes`).

#### Errors

- `XmlError` with [`XmlReason.DuplicateAttribute`](#XmlReason.DuplicateAttribute) if a name appears two times.
- `XmlError` with [`XmlReason.UndeclaredEntity`](#XmlReason.UndeclaredEntity) for a reference to another entity.
- `XmlError` with [`XmlReason.Limit`](#XmlReason.Limit) if `data` exceeds a bound of `limits`.
- `XmlError` with another kind if `data` does not match the grammar. `offset` counts bytes of
  `data`.
- `OutOfMemoryError` if the `Allocator` cannot supply the set.
